correctness.rationale: For n≥5 all nine Pn and five Qn exponent positions are distinct. Direct multiplication of (x^n+x+1)Qn gives nonunit middle coefficients 3x^n+2x^(n+1)+2x^(n+2); at x=3 their sum is exactly 3^(n+3), producing Pn(3)=(3^n+4)Qn(3). Since Pn(1)=9 and Qn(1)=5, polynomial divisibility Qn|Pn in Z[x] is impossible (would force integer quotient evaluation at 1). Q=1 yields universal type. The prior only-universal assertion for 3^n+1 is clearly attributed to Anders et al Theorem 2.4(1). Independent exact integer checks for n=5,6,7,11,52 corroborate, with all-n identity a symbolic proof, not a finite extrapolation.
residual_risks: The theorem claims uniform existence, not minimal nine/five support sizes, all representations or other bases.
